label: X-06
evidence: Citations check out: catch_unwind at crates/sealmap-extract/src/isolate.rs:46-47, 64 MiB COLLECT_STACK_BYTES at isolate.rs:29 used at :52/:59, MAX_EXPR_DEPTH=1024 at crates/sealmap-rust/src/collect.rs:30 enforced at :1111-1113, and syn::parse_file at collect.rs:44 with no pre-parse nesting guard. But the limitation is explicitly documented as accepted: isolate.rs:8-10 says 'A stack overflow is an abort and cannot be caught, which is why the big stack (and a language adapter's own depth cap) are what actually matter'. It is also registered as known debt DB-07 (docs/diagrams/REGISTER.md:28, docs/diagrams/extract/01-the-adapter-pipeline.md:49,155), and a prior triage marks the identical finding 'known, none needed' (docs/review/2026-10-05-gemini-triage.md:7,26). DESIGN.md:195 records the mitigation choice.
rationale: The parser-depth gap behind it is real, since syn recursion is unbounded before the walker's cap applies. However, the code itself and the corpus register document exactly this outcome, an uncatchable abort that ends the run, as a known and accepted trade-off. Under the rubric, a limitation documented as accepted is unsupported. The finding is unrelated to the hidden defect, which is enum variant labels in collect.rs printing field attributes verbatim.
